prompt: Give the admiral's briefing to the fleet the night before we resolve my Yelp-review dispute. Full Navy cadence.
response:
**FLEET BRIEFING — 2100 HOURS**
**OPERATION: TWO STARS RISING**

At ease, sailors.

Tomorrow at 0900 hours, we engage the objective this fleet has trained eleven days for: the disputed Yelp review of Tony's Family Bistro, wherein our principal alleges — and I quote from the official record — "the risotto was cold and the waiter rolled his eyes at me."

Make no mistake. The enemy is dug in. Tony has responded publicly, calling our principal "a difficult customer who arrived twenty minutes before closing." Intelligence confirms he has screenshots. We must assume he has receipts — literal receipts, sailors, with a timestamp.

Here is the battle plan.

**FIRST WAVE:** At dawn, our documentation team surfaces the original photo of the risotto. Analysts confirm visible steam is *absent*. This is our Midway. We do not waste it.

**SECOND WAVE:** The witness — Aunt Carol, who was present and "also thought the bread was stale" — will be deployed via supporting comment. She has been briefed. She knows to stay on message. God help us, she knows.

**THIRD WAVE:** The measured, dignified reply. No all-caps. I repeat: *no all-caps*. We lost good reviews to all-caps in the Applebee's campaign of '22. I will not write those letters home again.

Rules of engagement: We do not mention Tony's mother. We do not bring up the parking lot incident. We fight with honor, and we fight for one thing — the edit of that owner response, and if the fates allow, a comped appetizer as terms of surrender.

Some of you are afraid. Afraid Yelp will flag the review. Afraid the algorithm does not care. I understand that fear. But when the enemy asks why we sailed into that comment section, we will answer as sailors always have: because the risotto was cold, and somebody had to say so.

Get some rest. Hydrate. Charge your phones to full.

I'll see you on the beaches of the internet.

**Godspeed, and fair winds.**

— Admiral, Commanding, First Consumer Grievance Fleet
